title: Renglo ontology
description: A Renglo ontology. It names types, groups the instantiable ones into functional domains, and declares the relationships that may connect them. Property names are a closed set. The server also requires one type with no parent_type when node_types is not empty, a parent_type that names another type, no parent cycles, unique type names and semantics, and every instantiable type in exactly one domain. A domain type list cannot include an abstract type. relationship_class names a relationship class, and edge_taxonomy names an edge taxonomy. When both directions of a relationship are listed, their labels and semantics reverse each other. canonical_alignment and rules cite types and relationships that exist in this document, and a rule triple is listed once.

name.description: Stable document name. A letter followed by letters, digits, underscores, or dots, such as animals.ontology.

description.description: Which subjects this ontology covers. May be empty on a new draft.

dictionaries.description: Dictionary ids that map external names into these types, such as animals.1.0.0. Cite each id once.

classification_policy.description: How an instance receives its functional_domain.

description.description: What functional_domain means in this ontology. May be empty on a new draft.

derivation.description: How the domain is chosen. Membership in functional_domains[].types, or a walk up parent_type. May be empty on a new draft.

relationship_classes.description: Provenance of an edge: where the fact came from. Ids are unique.

node_types.description: The is-a tree. One entry is the root and has no parent_type. Abstract entries are not instantiated. type and semantic are unique.

functional_domains.description: A partition of the instantiable types. Each instantiable type appears in exactly one domain. A domain may follow parent_type, or cut across it. id and semantic are unique.

relationship_types.description: Directed relationships and the inverse of each. label and semantic are unique.

canonical_alignment.description: A specialized label aligned to a preferred label when both assert the same kind of fact. Each label appears once, and both labels are relationship types.

rules.description: Legal source type, relationship, and target type triples. Types and relationship labels come from this document.

edge_taxonomies.description: How a hop counts during traversal. A lower default_weight matters more. Ids are unique.

version.description: x.y.z while the ontology is a draft. A semantic version after publish.

origin.description: URI of the ontology this copy was cloned from. Empty when the ontology was created here.

semantic.description: A dotted name, such as animals.mammal or animals.domain.chordate.

id.description: Class id stored on a relationship type, such as structural or interaction.

type.description: Universal type name stored on a graph node.

parent_type.description: The type this one specializes. Omit it on the single root. It names another type in node_types.

abstract.description: True on a facet that must not be instantiated. Omit it, or set false, on an instantiable type.

examples.description: External names that dictionaries map into this type. Empty on an abstract type.

semantic.description: Identity of the branch. Often the same semantic as the abstract parent named by root_type.

root_type.description: A node type in this ontology, usually the abstract facet for the branch.

types.description: Instantiable node types in this domain. Each name is a node type, none of them abstract, and none repeated.

reverse_label.description: Label of the inverse edge. When that label has its own entry, the two entries reverse each other.

canonical_label.description: Preferred relationship label for the same fact.

source_type.description: A node type in this ontology.

relationship.description: A relationship label in this ontology.

target_type.description: A node type in this ontology.

default_weight.description: Traversal cost. Zero or greater. A lower weight is a hop that matters more.

examples.name: food.groups
examples.description: Edible things grouped for a menu.
